title: Modi's Biggest Cabinet Shake-Up in a Decade Could Replace His Finance and Education Ministers This Week
excerpt: Nirmala Sitharaman may lose the finance portfolio she has held for seven years, Dharmendra Pradhan faces removal over the NEET crisis, and the reshuffle is being designed for 2027 state elections.
body:
India is bracing for the most consequential cabinet reshuffle since Narendra Modi took office for a third term in June 2024. Multiple reports from national media outlets say the shake-up could come **as early as Monday**, just ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament — and it may redraw the faces behind some of the country's most powerful ministries.

Home Minister Amit Shah has reportedly already met President Droupadi Murmu to communicate the contours of the reorganisation, according to Gulte, citing national media correspondents. No official confirmation has come from the government, but the sheer volume of sourced reporting — and the political logic behind it — makes the reshuffle feel less like speculation and more like choreography.

## Sitharaman and Pradhan in the Crosshairs

The two names generating the most chatter are **Nirmala Sitharaman**, who has held the finance portfolio for nearly seven straight years, and **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the education minister who has been under fire for the NEET question paper leak and a broader crisis of confidence in India's examination system.

Sitharaman is not expected to leave cabinet entirely — reports suggest she may be moved to the Human Resources Development ministry, a significant demotion from the finance chair she has occupied since 2019. Her tenure has been polarising: she presided over the post-Covid economic recovery, pushed through GST reforms, and slashed corporate tax rates, but also drew persistent criticism on social media over GST on essentials and the perceived disconnect between government economic messaging and middle-class anxiety.

Pradhan's situation is reportedly more dire. The NEET paper leak scandals — which sparked nationwide protests, a 40-day march by students, and a "Cockroach Janta Party" campaign that went viral — have made his position untenable. Reports suggest he may be removed from the cabinet altogether and sent back to organisational work in the BJP.



> **"The NEET paper leak scandals — which sparked nationwide protests, a 40-day march by students, and a "Cockroach Janta Party" campaign that went viral — have made his position untenable."**


## The Political Math

The reshuffle is not just about competence reviews. It is fundamentally about **2027**, when seven states — including Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, and Gujarat — go to the polls. The BJP's organisational leadership, under the new party president, is pushing for greater representation of youth leaders under 50 and more women in ministerial roles.

The current cabinet has 72 ministers against a constitutional limit of 81, leaving room for up to nine new inductions. Several names are circulating, including leaders from UP, Rajasthan, and Bihar who could shore up the BJP's caste arithmetic ahead of the most consequential state election cycle of this decade.


![Narendra Modi — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5f/The_official_portrait_of_Shri_Narendra_Modi%2C_the_Prime_Minister_of_the_Republic_of_India.jpg)


The Monsoon Session itself provides political cover: by reshuffling before Parliament convenes, Modi can present the new team as a fresh start while deflecting opposition attacks on incumbents who have become liabilities.

## What It Means for NRIs

For the Indian diaspora, the finance ministry is the portfolio that matters most. From NRI deposit schemes to FCNR interest rates, from capital gains tax exemptions on government bonds to the rules governing foreign direct investment — every major NRI financial decision runs through North Block.

The RBI only days ago made dollar deposits significantly more attractive for non-resident Indians, offering yields approaching 6%. A new finance minister could accelerate — or quietly shelve — the liberalisation streak that has defined recent NRI-facing policy.

If Sitharaman moves, the question is not just who replaces her, but whether the replacement will continue the technocratic, reform-oriented approach she championed or tilt toward a more populist fiscal posture ahead of 2027. Names like **Piyush Goyal** and **Jayant Sinha** have surfaced in speculation, though neither has been confirmed.

## The Bigger Signal

Modi's third-term cabinet has been remarkably static compared to his first two. That stability was read as a sign of confidence. The fact that it is now being disrupted — and that the disruption is being framed as necessary — says something about where the BJP believes it is vulnerable.

Education, finance, and caste representation are not separate issues. They are the three threads that run through every Indian election, and the reshuffle is an attempt to retie them before the knot loosens further.

The official announcement, when it comes, will be watched not just for who gets which portfolio, but for what it reveals about Modi's own reading of his government's weaknesses — and how much political capital he is willing to spend to fix them before 2027.

*Sources: Gulte, India Today, PTI reports via Reuters*
